name: Mountain of Sustenance
significance: The Mountain of Sustenance is significant because it represents the origin of maize, the staple food of the Maya, and its discovery enabled the creation of humans and the development of Maya civilization.
location: Mythological realm; the concealed place of maize.

associations.name: Maize
associations.significance: Maize is the primary element associated with the Mountain of Sustenance, representing the source of life and sustenance for the Maya.

associations.name: Abundance

associations.name: Lightning
associations.significance: Lightning is associated with the opening of the mountain, representing the power of the gods to reveal the hidden maize.

description: The Mountain of Sustenance, also known as Paxil and Cayala, is a pivotal location in Maya mythology, particularly as recounted in the Popol Vuh, the sacred book of the K'iche' Maya. It represents the hidden source of maize, the life-sustaining crop that forms the basis of Maya civilization. Before the creation of humans from maize dough, the gods searched for a reliable food source. This search led them to the Mountain of Sustenance, a place of abundance where the precious kernels were concealed. The mountain's discovery and subsequent opening by the creator gods – Huracan, Tepeu, and Gucumatz – marked a turning point in the Maya creation narrative, enabling the creation of true humans capable of worshipping the gods. The mountain symbolizes not only the physical sustenance necessary for life but also the divine gift that allowed for the development of Maya culture and society. The opening of the mountain is often depicted as a transformative event, bringing forth not just maize but also other essential food sources like beans and cacao.
inhabitants: Initially, the mountain was guarded by forces that kept the maize hidden.
After the opening, it is conceptually inhabited by the spirit of sustenance and abundance.

companions.name: Huracan

companions.name: Tepeu and Gucumatz

cross_cultural_parallels.name: Corn Mother

cross_cultural_parallels.similarity: While not directly related to food, Mount Meru represents the center of the cosmos and a source of abundance and prosperity.

worshipPractices.description: Offerings of maize and other agricultural products were made to the gods to ensure continued abundance and a successful harvest.

extendedContent.title: Origins & Mythology
extendedContent.content: The origin of the Mountain of Sustenance is deeply intertwined with the Maya creation myth as described in the Popol Vuh. After several failed attempts to create humans, the gods realized they needed a reliable source of food. The animals revealed the existence of Paxil and Cayala, the Mountain of Sustenance, where maize was hidden. The mountain was initially difficult to access, requiring the combined efforts of the gods. The opening of the mountain involved breaking it apart, often attributed to lightning strikes orchestrated by the gods, particularly Huracan (Heart of Sky). This act unleashed the maize and other essential foods, allowing the gods to finally create humans from maize dough, thus establishing the foundation of Maya society and culture. The myth emphasizes the divine gift of sustenance and the importance of maize in Maya cosmology.

extendedContent.title: Role & Significance
extendedContent.content: The Mountain of Sustenance plays a crucial role in Maya religion and culture. It is not merely a geographical location but a symbolic representation of divine provision and the source of life. The discovery and opening of the mountain legitimized the role of maize as the primary food source and reinforced its sacred status. Rituals and ceremonies often centered around maize, reflecting its importance in daily life and its connection to the divine. The myth of the Mountain of Sustenance served to explain the origin of food and the relationship between humans and the gods, emphasizing the need for gratitude and reverence towards the natural world. The mountain is also significant as it represents the transformative power of the gods and their ability to provide for their creation.

extendedContent.title: Symbolism & Interpretation
extendedContent.content: The Mountain of Sustenance is rich in symbolic meaning. It represents not only physical sustenance but also spiritual nourishment and cultural identity. The hidden nature of the maize symbolizes the challenges and efforts required to obtain life's necessities. The opening of the mountain can be interpreted as a metaphor for divine intervention and the unlocking of potential. Maize itself symbolizes fertility, growth, and renewal, reflecting the cyclical nature of life and the agricultural cycle. The mountain's association with abundance also highlights the importance of community and sharing, as the maize was intended for all humankind. The Mountain of Sustenance can also be seen as a representation of the earth itself, a fertile source of life and sustenance.

extendedContent.title: Legacy & Influence
extendedContent.content: The myth of the Mountain of Sustenance continues to resonate in modern Maya culture and beyond. It serves as a reminder of the importance of maize and its connection to cultural identity. In contemporary Maya communities, maize continues to be a staple food and a central element in traditional ceremonies and rituals. The story of the Mountain of Sustenance is often retold and reinterpreted, reinforcing its cultural significance. The myth has also influenced artistic expression, with depictions of the mountain and the discovery of maize appearing in various forms of Maya art and literature. Furthermore, the story has gained recognition in broader cultural contexts, highlighting the rich mythology and cultural heritage of the Maya civilization. The concept of a hidden source of sustenance continues to inspire themes of discovery, abundance, and the importance of respecting natural resources.

shortDescription: A mythical mountain where maize, the staple food of the Maya, was hidden before being discovered and revealed to humankind.
subtitle: The Source of Life, Hidden in Stone
